title: Effect of Anifrolumab on Arterial Inflammation in Systemic Lupus Erythematosus Study
off: Effect of Anifrolumab on Arterial Inflammation in Systemic Lupus Erythematosus (AISLE) Study
collabs: Cambridge University Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust

officials.n: Jason M Tarkin, PhD MBBS FRCP

summary: People with systemic lupus erythematous (SLE) have an increased risk of premature atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease, which is believed to be caused by arterial inflammation. The aim of this study is to investigate the effects an interferon-targeting drug (anifrolumab) used for the treatment of active SLE on arterial inflammation. Arterial inflammation will be measured at baseline and after 4 months of treatment using Positron Emission Tomography (PET)/ Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI) with a radio-labelled tracer (68Ga-DOTATATE). Inflammation assessed by PET/MRI will also be compared with clinical disease activity, inflammatory blood markers and in patients with and without coronary artery disease on computed tomography coronary angiography (CTCA) and/or myocardial involvement on MRI.
desc:
It is known that people with SLE are at increased risk of cardiovascular disease because of ongoing inflammation in the body, but the effects of SLE therapies that target inflammation on blood vessels are unknown. Women aged between 35 to 44 are 50 times more likely to have a heart attack than their peers. The risk of stroke, peripheral vascular disease and heart failure is also increased by 2 to 3 fold.

The AISLE study aims to investigate the effects of treating active SLE with an interferon receptor inhibitor (anifrolumab) on arterial inflammation using 68Ga-DOTATATE PET/MRI. Our previous research has shown this imaging method to be effective for tracking macrophage-related arterial inflammation in the cardiovascular system. Patients with active SLE and a clinical SLE Disease Activity Index (SLEDAI) score of ≥4 who meet the eligibility criteria will be invited to participate in the study. All participants will receive anifrolumab therapy in addition to their current SLE treatments, for a total duration of 16 weeks, with imaging performed at baseline and at the end of treatment. CTCA will also be performed, as well as blood sampling for markers of inflammation.

This study will provide valuable information about the effects of anifrolumab on blood vessel inflammation in patients with SLE measured by PET imaging. We expect that this research will also contribute to the wider understanding of how inflammation lowering drugs could be used in general cardiovascular patients to prevent future heart attacks and strokes.
elig:
Inclusion Criteria:

1. Male or female participants 18 to 70 years of age
2. Able to give written, informed consent and to lie flat for scanning
3. Fulfil American College of Rheumatology/European Alliance of Associations for Rheumatology 2019 classification criteria for SLE
4. Current antinuclear antibody positive (ANA-ELISA ≥1.0, ANA Hep2 positivity)
5. Have ≥4 points on the clinical SLEDAI-2K disease activity score
6. Stable standard of care SLE therapies for ≥4 weeks
7. Prednisolone dosage ≤7.5 mg (or equivalent) daily
8. Up to date on required vaccinations (e.g., pneumonia, varicella zoster, and influenza \[inactivated/recombinant\]) prior to study entry

Exclusion Criteria:

1. Women of child-bearing potential not using adequate contraception
2. Breastfeeding
3. Already taking anifrolumab
4. Allergy and/or contraindication to anifrolumab or excipients
5. Anaphylaxis to any human gamma globulin therapy
6. History of recurrent infections requiring hospitalisation and intravenous (IV) antibiotics (e.g., 3 or more of the same type of infection over the previous 52 weeks)
7. Active Hepatitis B virus (HBV) or Hepatitis C virus (HCV) infection, confirmed by (a) HBsAg; or (b) HBcAb and HBV DNA detected above the lower limit of quantitation by reflex testing; or (c) HCV RNA
8. Any severe case of herpes zoster (HZ) infection, including, but not limited to: (a) systemic HZ such as herpes encephalitis or ophthalmic herpes involving the retina at any time prior to signing the ICF; (b) recurrent cutaneous HZ defined as 2 or more episodes within 2 years prior to signing the ICF; (c) any HZ infection that has not completely resolved within 12 weeks prior to signing the ICF
9. Any active cytomegalovirus or Epstein-Barr virus infection that has not completely resolved within 12 weeks prior to signing the ICF.
10. Opportunistic infection requiring hospitalization or IV antimicrobial treatment within 3 years prior to signing the ICF
11. Any of the following infections: (a) clinically significant chronic infection (i.e., osteomyelitis, bronchiectasis, etc) within 8 weeks prior to signing the ICF (chronic nail infections are allowed); (b) any infection requiring hospitalization or treatment with IV anti-infectives not completed at least 4 weeks prior to signing the ICF; (c) any infection requiring oral anti-infectives (including antivirals) within 2 weeks prior to signing the ICF
12. Any live or attenuated vaccine within 8 weeks prior to signing the informed consent form (ICF). Administration of killed or subunit vaccines is acceptable
13. Immunocompromised (known history of a primary immunodeficiency, splenectomy, or any underlying condition that predisposes the participant to infection, or a positive result for human immunodeficiency virus)
14. History of active tuberculosis or latent tuberculosis in whom an adequate course of treatment could not be confirmed
15. History of cancer (other than squamous or basal cell carcinoma of the skin/cervical cancer in situ treated with curative therapy more than 3 months prior to signing the ICF)
16. Receiving other biological therapies or monoclonal antibodies
17. Received rituximab or obinutuzumab within the past 24 weeks
18. Received belimumab within the past 12 weeks

18\. Received cyclophosphamide in the past 6 months 19. Cardiovascular event ≤3 months 20. Contra-indication to MRI or CT scanning 21. Contrast allergy or contrast-nephropathy 22. Active nephritis (\>1g protein/24hr or albumin to creatine ratio \>100) 23. Active central nervous system lupus 24. Active myocarditis 25. Chronic kidney disease (eGFR \<30 mL/min/1.73 m2) 26. Any condition that, in the opinion of the Investigator, would with impact patient safety, ability to complete imaging, or interfere with the interpretation of the study findings

arms.d: In this single arm of the study patients with patients will undergoing PET/MRI before and after anifrolumab therapy

primary.m: Comparison of coronary artery 68Ga-DOTATATE maximum tissue-to-blood ratio (TBRmax) after 16 weeks of anifrolumab compared to baseline
primary.tf: Between baseline and following 16 weeks of anifrolumab therapy

x.titre: Effet de l'anifrolumab sur l'inflammation artérielle dans le lupus érythémateux systémique (AISLE)
x.question: L'anifrolumab réduit-il l'inflammation artérielle coronaire mesurée en TEP/IRM chez des patients ayant un lupus actif ?
x.contexte:
Les patients atteints de lupus érythémateux systémique (LES) ont un risque accru d'athérosclérose prématurée, probablement lié à l'inflammation artérielle chronique. Les femmes lupiques de 35 à 44 ans ont un risque d'infarctus très supérieur à celui de leurs pairs, et le risque d'AVC, d'artériopathie et d'insuffisance cardiaque est aussi augmenté.

L'anifrolumab, anti-récepteur de l'interféron de type I, est indiqué dans le LES actif. Son effet sur les vaisseaux est inconnu. L'étude AISLE, de l'université de Cambridge, utilise la TEP/IRM au 68Ga-DOTATATE, traceur des macrophages, pour mesurer l'inflammation artérielle avant et après 4 mois de traitement. Quinze patients avec un SLEDAI clinique ≥ 4 reçoivent l'anifrolumab en plus de leur traitement habituel. L'inflammation sera comparée à l'activité clinique, aux marqueurs sanguins, à la maladie coronaire en coroscanner et à l'atteinte myocardique en IRM.
x.interet: L'étude pourrait montrer un effet vasculaire de l'anifrolumab, au-delà du contrôle de l'activité lupique. L'effectif réduit et l'absence de groupe contrôle limitent les conclusions.
x.profil: Des adultes de 18 à 70 ans atteints de LES actif, traités par anifrolumab.
inclusion: Âge de 18 à 70 ans, capable de rester allongé pour l'imagerie
LES selon critères ACR/EULAR 2019, ANA positifs
Traitement du LES stable depuis ≥ 4 semaines
exclusion: Femme en âge de procréer sans contraception adéquate, ou allaitante
Traitement antérieur par anifrolumab, allergie ou contre-indication
Zona sévère ou récurrent, infection à CMV ou EBV non résolue
Infection opportuniste ou chronique significative récente

bras.traitement: Anifrolumab en plus du traitement habituel, TEP/IRM au 68Ga-DOTATATE avant et après traitement

x.critere: Variation du rapport tissu/sang maximal (TBRmax) du 68Ga-DOTATATE dans les coronaires entre l'inclusion et 16 semaines
